_comment: Curated staples no source database has. Read pipeline/consumer/custom.py for the rules. Each food is computed per 100 g from foods that exist in the library: components[].g is grams of that component per 100 g of the FINISHED food (water lost in reducing / drying / straining is a component amount above 100; water added is not listed). A nutrient is filled only when every component has it; fill (whitelist), omit (blacklist), adjust (multiplier after the sum) and kcal=atwater are explained in custom.py. Every filled nutrient is marked estimated. Proportions are typical home / commercial recipes, not a standard. New foods get a frozen id from config/food_ids.json on the next build; an existing id never changes.

foods.name: Sumac
foods.head: sumac
foods.recipe: No source database has sumac (dried, ground Rhus coriaria drupes). Energy, protein, carbohydrate, fibre and fat are the mean of two dried whole-fruit spices (ground allspice and paprika), the nearest data in foodpipe.
foods.limits: Micronutrients, fat split and sodium are left missing: the minerals and vitamins of a tannin-rich, acidic fruit are not predicted by allspice or paprika, and sold sumac is often salted. Treat the macros as a rough guide; sumac is used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: Za'atar
foods.head: za'atar

components.why: sumac's micronutrients are unknown; counting them as zero makes every za'atar micronutrient a lower bound (never an overstatement) that understates by at most sumac's 25 % share

foods.recipe: Dried thyme 35 %, toasted sesame seeds 30 %, sumac 25 %, salt 10 % (a typical Levantine blend by weight).
foods.limits: Micronutrients are lower bounds because sumac's are unknown (see the sumac entry). Sodium is dominated by the salt and is the most reliable number; real blends range from about 2 % to 12 % salt.

foods.name: Baharat (seven-spice blend)
foods.head: baharat
foods.recipe: Black pepper 30 %, paprika 25 %, cumin 15 %, coriander seed 10 %, cinnamon 8 %, clove 5 %, cardamom 4 %, nutmeg 3 % (a common Lebanese / Syrian seven-spice mix; households vary).
foods.limits: Only nutrients present in all eight spice records are filled.

foods.name: Kala namak (black salt)
foods.head: kala namak
foods.recipe: Kala namak is sodium chloride with sodium sulfate, iron and sulfur compounds, so sodium is taken from table salt (the sodium content of both is within about 10 %) and energy and macronutrients are zero.
foods.limits: Its trace minerals (iron, sulfur) differ from table salt and are left missing.

foods.name: Amchur (dried green mango powder)
foods.head: amchur

components.note: raw unripe mango at 84.3 % water, dried to 8 % water: 100 x 92 / 15.7

foods.recipe: Amchur is sun-dried unripe mango ground to a powder. Raw unripe mango (water 84.3 g per 100 g in CoFID) is concentrated to 8 % water, which is 5.86 g of raw flesh per gram of powder; macronutrients, fibre and minerals scale with the dry matter.
foods.limits: Vitamins are left missing: the sun-drying and storage losses of vitamin C, carotenoids and the B vitamins are large and unmeasured. The final moisture (8 %) is an assumption; commercial powders run about 5 to 10 %.

foods.name: Ajwain (carom seeds)
foods.head: ajwain
foods.recipe: No source database has ajwain. It is a small Apiaceae seed like cumin and caraway, so energy, protein, carbohydrate and fat are the mean of cumin seed and caraway seed.
foods.limits: Fibre, fat split and every micronutrient are left missing: cumin and caraway differ from each other (fibre 10.5 g against 38 g) by more than the spread that would let the mean stand in for ajwain.

foods.name: Chaat masala
foods.head: chaat masala

components.why: ajwain's sodium is unknown; its cumin and caraway relatives carry 17 to 168 mg per 100 g, so at a 3 % share the omission is under 5 mg per 100 g of the blend and the sodium stays a lower bound

foods.recipe: Amchur 25 %, kala namak 15 %, roasted cumin 22 %, coriander seed 10 %, dried ginger 9 %, black pepper 6 %, dried red chili 5 %, ajwain 3 %, dried mint 5 % (a typical North Indian chaat masala; asafoetida, usually about 1 %, is left out).
foods.limits: Because amchur, kala namak and ajwain carry few nutrients here, only energy, protein, carbohydrate, fat and sodium are filled (sodium is dominated by the kala namak).

foods.name: Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves)
foods.head: kasuri methi

components.note: raw leaves at 87.6 % water, dried to 8 % water: 100 x 92 / 12.4

foods.recipe: Kasuri methi is fenugreek leaves dried to a crumbly herb. Raw leaves (water 87.6 g per 100 g in CoFID) are concentrated to 8 % water, which is 7.42 g of raw leaves per gram of dried herb; macronutrients and minerals scale with the dry matter.
foods.limits: Vitamins other than K (heat- and light-labile) are left missing. Fibre is not in the source. The 8 % final moisture is an assumption. Protein (34 g per 100 g) is probably 10 to 40 % high: the CoFID raw leaf is unusually protein-rich (4.6 g) and dried leafy herbs in the library sit at 20 to 22 g (dried coriander leaf, dried mint); a teaspoon of kasuri methi is about 1 g, so the effect on a recipe is under 0.4 g of protein.

foods.name: Kashmiri chili powder
foods.head: kashmiri chili powder
foods.recipe: Kashmiri chili powder is dried red chilies ground to a fine powder, so it takes the values of dried red chili pepper. The library's 'Chili powder' is a seasoning blend (cumin, garlic, oregano and salt, 2,867 mg sodium per 100 g) and would overstate sodium.
foods.limits: Kashmiri chilies are mild and thin-fleshed; capsaicin does not matter here but the fibre and mineral content of this generic dried chili may differ a little.

foods.name: Gochugaru (Korean red chili flakes)
foods.head: gochugaru
foods.recipe: Gochugaru is sun-dried Korean red chilies, coarsely ground or flaked, so it takes the values of dried red chili pepper (the same record as Kashmiri chili powder).
foods.limits: Korean chilies are mildly hot and fleshy; the generic dried red chili stands in for them.

foods.name: Doenjang (Korean soybean paste)
foods.head: doenjang
foods.recipe: Doenjang is a salty fermented soybean paste, the Korean counterpart of miso, so it takes the values of miso (soybeans, salt and a grain or no grain starter).
foods.limits: Doenjang is usually saltier and a little higher in protein than miso; sodium and protein are probably understated by 10 to 20 %. Check the label of a specific brand.

foods.name: Gochujang (Korean chili paste)
foods.head: gochujang
foods.recipe: Red chili 15 %, glutinous rice 20 % (dry weight; it is saccharified during fermentation, which does not change the energy), fermented soybean paste 25 %, salt 4 %, sugar 6 %, the rest (30 %) water: a typical commercial paste, about 190 kcal and 2.5 g sodium per 100 g.
foods.limits: Commercial pastes differ a lot in sugar, syrup and salt; read the label for a specific brand. Fermentation changes are ignored.

foods.name: Berbere (Ethiopian spice blend)
foods.head: berbere
foods.recipe: Dried red chili 40 %, paprika 25 %, ginger 8 %, garlic powder 6 %, fenugreek 4 %, coriander 4 %, cardamom 2 %, black pepper 2 %, clove, allspice, cinnamon and nutmeg 1 % each, salt 5 % (a typical mix; Ethiopian households vary and some add korarima, ajwain or rue).
foods.limits: Only nutrients present in all twelve component records are filled.

foods.name: Ras el hanout
foods.head: ras el hanout
foods.recipe: Cumin 20 %, coriander 15 %, ginger 15 %, turmeric 10 %, cinnamon 10 %, paprika 10 %, black pepper 8 %, cardamom 5 %, allspice 3 %, clove 2 %, nutmeg 2 % (the common Moroccan household mix; shop blends can carry thirty ingredients, including rose petals and lavender, which are left out).
foods.limits: Only nutrients present in all eleven component records are filled.

foods.name: Pomegranate molasses
foods.head: pomegranate molasses
foods.recipe: Pomegranate molasses is pomegranate juice boiled down; 350 g of juice makes 100 g, so sugars, energy and minerals are 3.5 times those of the juice.
foods.limits: Vitamins are left missing (vitamin C and folate are lost in boiling). Commercial products are often reduced further (about 65 % sugar, 4.5 to 5 x) and some add sugar or citric acid, so energy and carbohydrate here are on the low side.

foods.name: Tamarind paste
foods.head: tamarind paste

components.note: pulp; the other 40 g is water

foods.recipe: Tamarind paste is seedless tamarind pulp softened with water; 60 g of pulp and 40 g of water per 100 g gives a thick paste (pulp and water 3 : 2).
foods.limits: Commercial pastes and concentrates range from a thick pulp to a thin liquid, and some carry salt or sugar; this is the thick, unsalted kind. Vitamin C and folate are left missing.

foods.name: Labneh (strained yogurt)
foods.head: labneh

components.note: strained further: 140 g of Greek yogurt per 100 g of labneh

foods.recipe: Labneh is yogurt strained until firm. Whole-milk Greek yogurt (about 81 % water) strained to about 74 % water is 1.4 times as concentrated, so protein, fat (and its fatty-acid split), calcium, phosphorus and vitamin A are 1.4 times Greek yogurt. Lactose drains with the whey: it stays at the same concentration in a smaller water phase, so per 100 g it falls to about 0.9 of the yogurt's (0.65 of the 1.4x figure), which lowers carbohydrate and sugar. Energy is recomputed from the macros (4/9/4).
foods.limits: Whey-soluble nutrients (potassium, B2, B12, sodium) are left missing because how much drains varies; many labnehs also carry salt and are stored under olive oil, which this does not include.

foods.name: Loomi (dried black lime)
foods.head: loomi

components.note: fresh lime is 88 % water; loomi about 10 %, so 770 g of fresh lime dries to 100 g

foods.recipe: Loomi is whole lime boiled briefly in brine and sun-dried until black and hollow. Values are fresh lime concentrated by its lost water (770 g fresh per 100 g dried).
foods.limits: Vitamin C, folate and thiamin are left missing because drying in the sun destroys an unknown share of them. Brined loomi carries some salt that is not counted. It is used one or two at a time, so its nutrients barely matter.

foods.name: Rose water
foods.head: rose water
foods.recipe: Rose water is a steam distillate of rose petals: water with aroma compounds and no meaningful energy or nutrients, so it takes the values of water.
foods.limits: Only energy and macronutrients (all zero) are given. Used by the teaspoon for aroma.

foods.name: Date syrup (dibs)
foods.head: date syrup

components.note: dates are pressed and the juice reduced; the fibre stays in the pulp

foods.recipe: Date syrup is the juice of cooked dates, strained and reduced to a thick syrup. Values are dried dates per 105 g with the fibre removed (it stays behind in the pressed pulp), energy recomputed.
foods.limits: Minerals are assumed to pass into the juice in full, so potassium and iron are probably overstated by 10 to 30 %. Brands vary in thickness.

foods.name: Sichuan peppercorn
foods.head: sichuan peppercorn
foods.recipe: No source database has Sichuan peppercorn (the dried husks of Zanthoxylum). Energy and macronutrients are the mean of two dried berry and seed spices, black pepper and coriander seed.
foods.limits: Micronutrients and the fat split are left missing. Used by the half teaspoon, so only the macros could matter, and barely.

foods.name: Star anise
foods.head: star anise
foods.recipe: No source database has star anise (Illicium verum). It takes the energy and macronutrients of anise seed, a dried aromatic fruit with the same flavour compound (anethole).
foods.limits: Micronutrients and the fat split are left missing; a pod weighs half a gram.

foods.name: Chinese five-spice powder
foods.head: five spice
foods.recipe: A common home ratio: star anise 30, cassia or cinnamon 25, fennel seed 20, Sichuan peppercorn 15, cloves 10.
foods.limits: Only energy and macronutrients, because two components carry macros only. Used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: Fermented black beans (douchi)
foods.head: fermented black beans
foods.recipe: Douchi are black soybeans fermented with a mould, salted and partly dried. Values are dried fermented soybeans (70 g), salt (10 g) and moisture (20 g) per 100 g.
foods.limits: Vitamin K is left out (the natto proxy is rich in K2 from a bacterium douchi doesn't use). Sodium varies a lot by brand; rinsing before use, as many cooks do, removes some of it.

foods.name: Ancho chile, dried
foods.head: ancho chile

components.note: another dried Mexican chile of the same kind

foods.recipe: Ancho is a dried ripe poblano. It takes the values of dried pasilla chile, the nearest dried Mexican chile in the source data (both are mild, wrinkled, raisin-sweet dried chiles).
foods.limits: Vitamin C is left missing because it varies widely with drying. Anchos are a little milder and fleshier than pasillas.

foods.name: Guajillo chile, dried
foods.head: guajillo chile
foods.recipe: Guajillo is a dried mirasol chile, thin-skinned and bright red. Values are the mean of sun-dried red chile and dried pasilla chile.
foods.limits: Vitamin C is left missing because it varies widely with drying.

foods.name: Chipotle peppers in adobo sauce
foods.head: chipotle in adobo
foods.recipe: A typical canned chipotles en adobo: smoked dried jalapenos rehydrated in a thin sauce of tomato, vinegar, onion, garlic, a little sugar and salt (about 860 mg sodium per 100 g, close to common labels).
foods.limits: Brands vary in sugar and salt. Vitamin C is left missing.

foods.name: Achiote paste (recado rojo)
foods.head: achiote paste

components.note: stands in for ground annatto seed (similar dried seed spice macros)

foods.recipe: Recado rojo: ground annatto seed with vinegar or bitter orange, garlic, cumin, oregano, pepper and salt, pressed into a paste. Annatto seed itself is not in any source database, so paprika stands in for its share.
foods.limits: Only energy, macronutrients and sodium; annatto's micronutrients are not predicted by paprika. Used by the tablespoon for colour and flavour.

foods.name: Sambar powder
foods.head: sambar powder
foods.recipe: A Tamil home sambar powder: coriander seed, dried red chili, roasted toor and chana dal, cumin, fenugreek, black pepper, turmeric and curry leaves, dry-roasted and ground.
foods.limits: Recipes vary by household; some add hing, rice or mustard seed. Used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: Bisi bele bath powder
foods.head: bisi bele bath powder
foods.recipe: A Karnataka bisi bele bath powder: coriander seed, dried red chili, roasted chana and urad dal, dry coconut, cumin, fenugreek, cinnamon, cloves and pepper, roasted and ground.
foods.limits: Some recipes add poppy seeds, marathi moggu or kalpasi, which aren't in the source data. Used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: Rasam powder
foods.head: rasam powder
foods.recipe: A Tamil rasam powder: coriander seed, black pepper, cumin, dried red chili and a little toor dal, with turmeric and curry leaves, roasted and ground.
foods.limits: Recipes vary by household. Used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: Jaggery
foods.head: jaggery

components.note: the cane solids refined sugar loses

foods.recipe: Jaggery is whole cane juice boiled down without separating the molasses. Values are refined sugar with molasses added back (82 + 20 g per 100 g, the extra water boiled off), which lands on typical jaggery: about 380 kcal, a little iron, potassium and calcium.
foods.limits: Mineral content of real jaggery varies several-fold with the cane and the pan (iron especially); palm jaggery differs again. Treat the minerals as a rough middle.

foods.name: Injera (teff flatbread)
foods.head: injera

components.why: water in the fermented batter, most of it kept in the cooked bread

foods.recipe: Injera is a fermented batter of teff flour and water cooked on one side. 100 g of finished injera holds about 36 g of teff flour (a typical 1 : 2 flour-to-water batter, part of the water steaming off).
foods.limits: Fermentation changes some B vitamins and phytate (iron absorption improves) but not the totals much. Many North American injera are part wheat or barley flour; this is the all-teff kind.

foods.name: Galangal
foods.head: galangal
foods.recipe: No source database has galangal. It takes the energy and macronutrients of fresh ginger root, a close relative eaten the same way (sliced into soups and pastes).
foods.limits: Micronutrients are left missing. Used by the slice.

foods.name: Makrut lime leaves
foods.head: makrut lime leaves
foods.recipe: No source database has makrut lime leaves. They take the energy and macronutrients of raw citrus peel, the nearest aromatic citrus tissue.
foods.limits: Micronutrients are left missing; a few leaves weigh a gram or two, so they don't move the numbers.

foods.name: Scotch bonnet pepper
foods.head: scotch bonnet
foods.recipe: Scotch bonnet and habanero are Capsicum chinense chiles; they take the values of raw hot red chili pepper, which they match closely apart from heat.
foods.limits: Vitamin C varies with ripeness. Very hot: half a pepper seasons a pot.

foods.name: Culantro
foods.head: culantro
foods.recipe: Culantro (Eryngium foetidum) is a stronger cousin of cilantro used in the Caribbean and Vietnam; it takes the values of fresh cilantro.
foods.limits: A proxy: the leaves are tougher and likely a little higher in minerals. Used by the handful.

foods.name: Shrimp paste (belacan, terasi)
foods.head: shrimp paste
foods.recipe: Shrimp paste is tiny shrimp or krill salted, fermented and pressed. Values are dried shrimp (70 g), salt (15 g) and moisture (15 g) per 100 g, about 6 g sodium.
foods.limits: Brands range widely in salt and moisture; Filipino bagoong is wetter. Used by the teaspoon, and toasted before use.

foods.name: Whole-wheat couscous, dry
foods.head: whole-wheat couscous

components.note: cooked couscous is about 60 % water; 250 g cooked comes from 100 g dry

foods.recipe: Dry whole-wheat couscous is the cooked whole-wheat couscous in the source data with its cooking water taken back out (100 g dry swells to about 250 g cooked).
foods.limits: Any salt or fat added in the source's cooking method would be concentrated too; the source is the no-added-salt version. Water-soluble vitamins lost in cooking are not added back, so B vitamins are slightly understated.

foods.name: Orange blossom water
foods.head: orange blossom water
foods.recipe: Orange blossom water is a steam distillate of bitter-orange flowers: water with aroma and no meaningful nutrients, so it takes the values of water.
foods.limits: Only energy and macronutrients (all zero) are given. Used by the teaspoon for aroma.

foods.name: Thai basil
foods.head: thai basil
foods.recipe: Thai basil (Ocimum basilicum var. thyrsiflora) takes the values of sweet basil, the same species; only the aroma (anise and clove) differs.
foods.limits: A same-species proxy. Used by the handful.

foods.name: Holy basil
foods.head: holy basil
foods.recipe: Holy basil (Ocimum tenuiflorum) takes the values of sweet basil, a close relative of the same genus eaten the same way.
foods.limits: A same-genus proxy; minerals may differ a little. Used by the handful.

foods.name: Palm sugar
foods.head: palm sugar
foods.recipe: Palm sugar is palm sap boiled down without refining, the palm counterpart of cane jaggery; it takes the jaggery estimate.
foods.limits: Minerals vary with the palm and the pan; treat them as a rough middle. Used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: Niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced butter)
foods.head: niter kibbeh
foods.recipe: Butter clarified slowly with onion, garlic, ginger, fenugreek, cardamom (korerima), turmeric and pepper, then strained. Values are ghee with the strained-out aromatics' small share.
foods.limits: The aromatics are strained off, so their share is a rough guess; nutritionally this is ghee. Used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: Mitmita (Ethiopian chili blend)
foods.head: mitmita
foods.recipe: Mitmita: very hot dried bird's eye chili ground with korerima (Ethiopian cardamom), cloves and salt.
foods.limits: Very hot; used by the pinch. Household recipes vary in salt.

foods.name: Xawaash (Somali spice blend)
foods.head: xawaash
foods.recipe: A common Somali xawaash: cumin, coriander, black pepper, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and turmeric, toasted and ground.
foods.limits: Recipes vary by household. Used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: West Indian curry powder
foods.head: west indian curry powder
foods.recipe: A Jamaican and Trinidadian style curry powder: turmeric-forward, with coriander, cumin, fenugreek, mustard seed, fennel, allspice (pimento) and pepper.
foods.limits: Brands differ; some add salt or flour, this one has neither. Used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: Barberries, dried (zereshk)
foods.head: barberries
foods.recipe: No source database has dried barberries. They take the energy and macronutrients of dried cranberries, the nearest tart dried red berry.
foods.limits: Barberries are sold unsweetened and are sourer; sugars and micronutrients are left missing. Used by the spoonful, usually briefly fried with a pinch of sugar.

foods.name: Aleppo pepper (pul biber)
foods.head: aleppo pepper
foods.recipe: Pul biber is coarse, mildly hot, slightly salted dried red pepper. Values are paprika and sun-dried chili with a little salt.
foods.limits: Only energy, macronutrients and sodium; oil content varies by brand. Used by the teaspoon.

foods.name: Dukkah
foods.head: dukkah
foods.recipe: Egyptian dukkah: toasted hazelnuts and sesame pounded with coriander, cumin, pepper and salt.
foods.limits: Recipes vary (some use chickpeas or almonds). Used by the spoonful with bread and oil.

foods.name: Calamansi
foods.head: calamansi

components.note: a small sour citrus used the same way

foods.recipe: Calamansi is a small sour citrus squeezed like lime in Filipino and Malaysian cooking; it takes the values of lime.
foods.limits: A proxy; calamansi is a little sweeter and more aromatic. Used by the squeeze.

foods.name: Sambal oelek
foods.head: sambal oelek
foods.recipe: Sambal oelek is fresh red chili ground with a little vinegar and salt (about 2 g sodium per 100 g).
foods.limits: Vitamin C is left out because the paste is stored; brands vary in salt.

foods.name: Kecap manis (sweet soy sauce)
foods.head: kecap manis
foods.recipe: Kecap manis is soy sauce cooked down with palm sugar into a thick syrup. Values are soy sauce and palm sugar, reduced (105 g to 100 g).
foods.limits: Brands range in sweetness and salt; only energy, macros, sugar and sodium are given.

foods.name: Candlenut
foods.head: candlenut

components.note: a similar oily kernel used the same way

foods.recipe: Candlenut is an oily kernel ground into Indonesian and Malaysian spice pastes to thicken them; it takes the macronutrients of macadamia, the usual substitute.
foods.limits: Candlenut is higher in polyunsaturated fat than macadamia; the fat split is a rough guide. Never eaten raw in quantity; used 2 or 3 at a time, cooked.

foods.name: Ají amarillo paste
foods.head: aji amarillo
foods.recipe: Ají amarillo paste is the yellow Peruvian chili blended smooth with a little oil, vinegar and salt; the chili takes the values of fresh hot chili.
foods.limits: Vitamin C is left out (stored paste). Brands vary in salt and oil.

foods.name: Masarepa (precooked corn flour)
foods.head: masarepa
foods.recipe: Masarepa is white corn, degermed, cooked and milled. It takes the values of white corn flour.
foods.limits: Precooking changes little nutritionally. This is a refined corn flour (degermed), not whole grain.
